key_insight: A scaffold-aware foundation model pretrained on small-molecule natural products uses masked objectives and contrastive learning to produce representations that improve taxonomy classification, genome mining, and virtual screening performance.
problem_solved: Natural products have complex, diverse molecular scaffolds and limited labeled data for downstream tasks; existing models struggle to capture scaffold-specific features needed for taxonomy, biosynthetic gene cluster linking, and virtual screening in drug discovery.
method: Curate a large natural-product molecule corpus and pretrain a scaffold-aware encoder to emphasize core scaffold information.
Combine masked modeling objectives (to learn local and contextual chemical features) with contrastive learning (to align similar taxonomy/functional signals) during pretraining.
Fine-tune or apply the pretrained representations to downstream tasks—taxonomy classification, genome mining for biosynthetic gene clusters, and virtual screening—to demonstrate improved performance.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a domain-tailored foundation model that yields more transferable, scaffold-sensitive molecular representations—accelerating model development and improving accuracy across multiple drug-discovery tasks with less labeled data.
